rows.reply: Here is the graph of the square‑root function \(y=\sqrt{x}\). The horizontal axis is labelled **x** (the radicand) and the vertical axis is labelled **y** (the root). The curve starts at the origin \((0,0)\) and rises gently to the right, showing that for each non‑negative \(x\) there is exactly one non‑negative \(y\) such that \(y^{2}=x\). Notice the curve exists only for \(x\ge 0\); there is no part of the graph on the left side of the y‑axis because square roots of negative numbers are not real.
